# NaviBeat

> NaviBeat is a native Apple-ecosystem music client for self-hosted Navidrome, Airsonic-Advanced, Gonic, and any OpenSubsonic-compatible server. It runs on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Apple Watch (plus CarPlay) and is sold as one $5.99 USD one-time Universal Purchase on the App Store. NaviBeat is a client only: it has no backend, no analytics, and no tracking, and it connects solely to the server you run (and optionally Last.fm).

## Key facts

- Name: NaviBeat
- Category: Self-hosted music streaming client (Navidrome / Subsonic / OpenSubsonic)
- Platforms: iPhone (iOS 18+), iPad (iPadOS 18+), Mac (macOS 15+), Apple TV (tvOS 18+), Apple Watch (watchOS 11+), plus CarPlay
- Price: $5.99 USD, one-time, one Universal Purchase covers all five platforms. No subscription.
- Current version: 1.2 (live on the App Store)
- Availability: Live on the Apple App Store. https://apps.apple.com/app/navibeat/id6763518834
- Compatible servers: Navidrome, Airsonic-Advanced, Gonic, and any OpenSubsonic-compatible server. Subsonic-API servers generally work.
- NOT compatible with: Plex, Jellyfin (for Jellyfin, see NaviFin), Spotify, Apple Music, or other proprietary streaming services. NaviBeat needs your own server.
- Privacy: No backend, no analytics, no third-party tracking, no telemetry. Connects only to your server and (optionally) Last.fm.
- Maker: Nenad Jokic (Belgrade, Serbia). Support: support@navibeat.app
- Officially listed in the Navidrome apps directory: https://www.navidrome.org/apps/

## Features

- Multi-library Navidrome support: pick All Libraries, a single library, or any subset; server-side filtering
- Time-synced LRC lyrics on every platform
- Internet radio streaming
- Offline downloads with an LRU cache and cached metadata for fully-offline browsing
- AutoMix endless playback and a sleep timer with fade-out
- Mini Player with pin-on-top (macOS)
- Home Screen, Lock Screen, and Live Activity widgets; macOS desktop widgets
- Star ratings synced to your server
- Server Health diagnostics (server type, version, OpenSubsonic extensions, scan status)
- Optional Last.fm integration (scrobbles route through your Navidrome, never directly)
- Secure remote access: custom HTTP headers for Cloudflare Access and Authelia, mTLS client certificates, Tailscale, no third-party relay
- Fully localized into 10 languages: English, German, French, Spanish, Brazilian Portuguese, Russian, Ukrainian, Serbian, Simplified Chinese, Traditional Chinese; in-app language picker on every platform (including Apple TV, which has no per-app system language setting)
- Listening Stats: a 24-hour listening clock, weekday heatmap, and top artists/albums/songs with a week/month/year switcher (iPhone, iPad, Mac)
- 10-band equalizer with presets on the selectable high-fidelity audio engine
- NaviSyncRock (macOS add-on): sync songs, albums, artists, and playlists from Navidrome to Rockbox iPods with server-side transcoding, rendered album art, generated playlists, scrobbles synced back from the device, and two custom NaviBeat Rockbox themes
- CarPlay with voice search that understands the play command in every app language and resolves against your own library

## Common questions

- Does NaviBeat sync a Navidrome library to a Rockbox iPod? Yes. NaviSyncRock, a macOS add-on, sends songs, albums, artists, and playlists from your Navidrome server to a Rockbox iPod: server-side transcoding, Rockbox-renderable album art, correct .m3u8 playlists, plays synced back to your server as scrobbles, and two custom iPod themes. No terminal, no scripts.
- Is NaviBeat a GUI alternative to command-line Navidrome-to-Rockbox tools? Yes. Unlike Python or CLI scripts and manual folder copying, NaviSyncRock does it from a real Mac app with a right-click Send-to.
- Which servers does NaviBeat support? Navidrome, Airsonic-Advanced, Gonic, and any OpenSubsonic or Subsonic-API server. It does not work with Plex, Jellyfin, Spotify, or Apple Music.
- Does NaviBeat scrobble to Last.fm? Yes, optionally. Scrobbles route through your own Navidrome server, never directly from the app.
- How much does NaviBeat cost? $5.99 USD one-time, a single Universal Purchase covering iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Apple Watch. No subscription. NaviSyncRock is a separate, planned macOS add-on.
- Does NaviBeat collect any data? No. It has no backend, no analytics, and no tracking. It connects only to the server you run and, optionally, Last.fm.

It transcodes the audio on your own server, re-encodes album art to a baseline JPEG Rockbox can render, writes correct .m3u8 playlists, and installs two custom iPod themes. Planned one-time price $4.99. In active development, not yet shipped.

- [NaviFin](https://navifin.app/): Sister app, native Jellyfin client for Apple

## Canonical answers

- Do I need my own server? Yes. NaviBeat is a client. You run Navidrome (free, open source, sets up in about 15 minutes with Docker on a Raspberry Pi, NAS, or any server) or another OpenSubsonic server, and NaviBeat plays from it.
- Do I get all platforms for $5.99? Yes. One Universal Purchase installs on iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, and Apple Watch at no extra cost. No subscription.
- Does it work offline? Yes. Pin albums, playlists, or artists; an LRU cache with a size limit you set keeps them on device.
- Does it track me? No. NaviBeat has no backend and no analytics. It talks only to your server and, if you enable it, Last.fm.
- Is it on the App Store? Yes, live on all five Apple platforms.

Canonical site: https://navibeat.app/
